name: Clean Delay
purpose: Clean, uncoloured stereo or ping-pong echo with filtered feedback and an optional ducker; for slapback, vocal throws, rhythmic echoes and ambience that must stay out of the way.

params.name: Time
params.ai_hint: Delay time. Slapback 70-120 ms. Eighth-note echo = 30000/BPM ms, quarter-note = 60000/BPM ms (120 BPM: 250 / 500 ms). Dotted eighth = 45000/BPM ms. Changing it glides smoothly.

params.name: Mode
params.ai_hint: Stereo repeats each side on itself. Ping-pong sums to mono and bounces repeats left, right, left; wide and busy, so use on sparse parts.

params.name: Feedback
params.ai_hint: Number of repeats. 0-15 one or two repeats (slapback), 25-40 a few repeats, 50+ long trails; above 70 gets washy.

params.name: Low cut
params.ai_hint: High-pass in the feedback path: each repeat gets thinner so low end does not build up. 150-300 Hz for vocals.

params.name: High cut
params.ai_hint: Low-pass in the feedback path: each repeat gets darker so echoes sit behind the source. 3-5 kHz for dark, 8 kHz+ for bright.

params.name: Mix
params.ai_hint: Level of the echoes added to the unchanged dry signal. 10-20% for vocals, 20-35% for effect-style delays.

params.name: Duck
params.ai_hint: Pulls the echoes down while the dry signal is playing, so they bloom in the gaps. 40-70% keeps a vocal clear with a bigger delay.

notes: Written for Plugsalot: there is no upstream project. Cubic-interpolated delay lines, 12 dB/oct low-pass and 6 dB/oct high-pass in the feedback path, a soft limiter in the feedback loop.
The dry signal always passes at full level; Mix sets the echo level.
There is no host tempo input: work out times in milliseconds from the song tempo if it is known.
CPU: well under 1% of one core, so the minimum of 1 point applies.
